subject: Intermittent connection resets to private deployment — possible SNAT/MSS interaction
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmecorp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, infra-ops@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sporadic resets to the private deployment in our VPC (large requests)

Hi Rishi / team,

Since we moved traffic to the new private deployment (vpc-10a) we see intermittent TCP resets and 502s for large POSTs (payloads > 12KB) to your inference endpoints. It happens mostly during our nightly backup window (roughly 02:00-03:00 UTC) but we've also seen daytime hits.

Symptoms:
- Client gets connection reset or TLS connection aborted mid-transfer.
- Server logs show stalled TCP streams; sometimes we see retransmits and then a hard reset.
- When we limit the client MSS to ~1300 the failures drop dramatically.

What we tried:
- Adjusted client-side MTU/ MSS clamp on our edge appliances (reduced to 1300) — fewer failures but not zero.
- Rotated destination NAT to a different subset of IPs — same pattern.
- Captured a short pcap during failure window (attached).

We suspect either:
1) an asymmetric path where SNAT at TGW/edge rewrites ports and causes conntrack mismatch on return, or
2) an MTU/fragmentation issue where the middlebox drops fragments (we see DF=1 in some packets).

Attaching: acme_backup_window_20261202.pcap, acme_traceroute_12-02.txt

Can you take a look or advise on what runtime/network settings we should inspect on the Redwood side? We can open a maintenance window if you need to change routing or NAT behavior.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Site Reliability Engineer — Acme Corp

On Wed, Dec 2, 2026 at 4:05 PM Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jonas — can you check TGW routing and whether our egress nodes are doing SNAT for your prefix (10.0.0.0/8) during that window?

I pulled the control-plane logs and the node-level iptables rules for the dedicated pool that serves Acme traffic. Initial findings:

- We are doing SNAT for some outbound flows coming from the private pods to avoid leaking private source addresses across a transit GW we don't own. That SNAT uses a port range and relies on conntrack entries being created on the same egress node on return.
- The packet captures (thanks Samir) show the DF flag set on large packets and evidence of retransmits. I also see ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages on the path but they are only seen from an intermediate hop (your edge) back to the client, not from our egress — which suggests fragmentation is being blocked somewhere in the middle.
- There's an observable period where conntrack entries spike ~20k and then occasional port reuse/timeout on our SNAT pool — likely coinciding with your backup traffic.

Hypothesis: When the backup window runs, the snapshot/backup traffic uses many concurrent flows that consume the SNAT port range and/or evict conntrack entries, leading to asymmetric return paths or missing conntrack state — clients see resets. Combined with DF set and MTU mismatches, some responses may not be reassembled and are dropped.

Short actionable checks we can take now:
1) Increase conntrack max and timeout on the egress nodes to accommodate backup surge (temporary).
2) Temporarily exclude Acme's source prefix from SNAT on our egress nodes (preserve original source) if their network allows it — reduces state pressure.
3) Add MSS clamping on our egress for paths where DF is present (we can clamp to 1300) — this mitigates fragmentation drops.

Samir — can you confirm whether your edge allows us to accept non-SNATed source IPs from the Dedicated pool if we request it for the maintenance window? If not, we can do MSS clamp + conntrack tuning and test.

I'll prepare a short playbook we can run during the maintenance window.

-Jonas
Senior Network Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — that matches what we see on our side. A few clarifications:

- Our perimeter does enforce DF and drops fragments by default. We had previously tried MSS clamp at the edge but only on a subset of subnets. If Redwood can clamp to 1300 that will probably remove the majority of failures.
- We can allow non-SNATed traffic from your Dedicated pool if you provide the source prefix list and a time-limited window. We'd prefer to try conntrack tuning + MSS clamp first (lower blast radius).
- Uploaded an extended pcap to S3 with more flows during the backup spike: https://acme.s3.amazonaws.com/support/acme_backup_window_20261202.pcap
- Also included a traceroute that shows an intermediate hop returning "Fragmentation needed" (see acme_traceroute_12-02.txt).

If you can provision a short maintenance window Thu 2026-12-05 03:00-04:00 UTC, we'll monitor concurrently.

Samir

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Samir / team — thanks for the quick followups and the S3 link. Proposed remediation plan for the maintenance window (INFRA-2241):

Planned steps (Thu 2026-12-05 03:00-04:00 UTC):
1) Increase conntrack table and timeouts on the affected egress nodes: sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000 and increase tcp timeout for ESTABLISHED flows (Jonas to run).
2) Apply MSS clamp on egress for flows destined to Acme subnets: tc qdisc/netfilter-based clamp to 1300 (Jonas).
3) If conntrack tuning + MSS clamp reduces failures to acceptable levels, we will leave that configuration and re-evaluate SNAT exclusion.
4) If issues persist, we will request a temporary SNAT exclusion and provide the source CIDRs (we will coordinate exact prefixes before the window).
5) Post-change: run a full traffic replay from Samir's pcap in a test net and monitor for resets / conntrack evictions.

Marissa — I'll coordinate status updates and escalation if we see anomalies. Dev — please stand by to rollback sysctl + qdisc changes if any node degrades.

Samir, can you confirm the maintenance window and that you will monitor from your edge? Once you confirm, Jonas and I will schedule the change in the Jira and we'll post runbook steps.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
